sentences.en: In December 1958, the first conference of the Union of African Nations was held at Accra in Ghana.
sentences.zh: 1958年12月，首届非洲国家联盟会议在加纳阿克拉举行。

sentences.en: Among the delegations was one from Algeria, representatives of a movement which for four years had been engaged in the bloody war of independence from France.
sentences.zh: 与会代表团中有一个来自阿尔及利亚，他们代表着一场已经进行了四年、旨在脱离法国统治的血腥独立战争的运动。

sentences.en: But the Algerian delegates were not interested solely in Algeria.
sentences.zh: 但阿尔及利亚代表们关心的不仅仅是阿尔及利亚。

sentences.en: Every African must feel directly engaged and ready to answer the call of any and all territories, one of them declared.
sentences.zh: 其中一位代表宣称，每一位非洲人都必须感到自己直接参与其中，并随时准备响应任何及所有领土的号召。

sentences.en: An Algerian cannot be a true Algerian if he does not feel in his core the indescribable tragedy that is unfolding in the two Rhodesias or in Angola.
sentences.zh: 如果一个阿尔及利亚人不能从内心深处感受到正在两个罗得西亚或安哥拉上演的难以言表的悲剧，那他就不是一个真正的阿尔及利亚人。

sentences.en: And that man, Dominic, was Frantz Fanon, who I guess is, I mean, he's a colossally influential figure, isn't he,
sentences.zh: 那个人，多米尼克，就是弗朗茨·法农，我想他，我是说，他是一位影响力巨大的人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: on the history of decolonisation and I guess specifically in the African context.
sentences.zh: 在非殖民化历史上，我想特别是在非洲背景下。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So born in Martinique, he's one of the,
sentences.zh: 他出生于马提尼克，他是……

sentences.en: he becomes one of the emblematic intellectuals of the age of decolonisation with his arguments about blackness and about pan-Africanism and so on.
sentences.zh: 他成为了非殖民化时代最具代表性的知识分子之一，提出了关于黑人性、泛非主义等等的论点。

sentences.en: Now you, I know what you're thinking, Tom, you think I know nothing about Frantz Fanon.
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道你在想什么，汤姆，你以为我对弗朗茨·法农一无所知。

sentences.en: But what you don't know is that my very first work of research was on French colonial Algeria, a subject that Fanon came to know very well.
sentences.zh: 但你不知道的是，我的第一项研究工作就是关于法国殖民统治下的阿尔及利亚，这是一个法农非常了解的主题。

sentences.en: I wrote a thesis about an anti-Semitic riot in the city of Constantin in Algeria in 1934.
sentences.zh: 我写过一篇关于1934年阿尔及利亚君士坦丁市反犹太暴乱的论文。

sentences.en: Utterly unread, languishes somewhere in a library in Oxford, but I did it.
sentences.zh: 完全没人读过，在牛津大学的某个图书馆里落灰，但我确实写了。

sentences.en: So there you go.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是这样。

sentences.en: So I've managed to turn the conversation from Fanon to myself, which regular listeners will know is exactly the spirit in which we conduct this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我成功地把话题从法农转到了我自己身上，老听众都知道，这正是我们制作这档播客的精神所在。

sentences.en: A classic European manoeuvre.
sentences.zh: 典型的欧洲式操弄。

sentences.en: Very much.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Re-centering Europe.
sentences.zh: 重新以欧洲为中心。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: On what is going to be a discussion about the process of African decolonisation.
sentences.zh: 在这一场关于非洲非殖民化进程的讨论中。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a fascinating subject though, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是啊，不过这是一个引人入胜的话题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and Fanon's a remarkable writer, The Wretched of the Earth, I mean, is kind of one of the great kind of foundational texts.
sentences.zh: 是的，法农是一位了不起的作家，《全世界受苦的人》可以说是最伟大的奠基性著作之一。

sentences.en: But I think one of the things that's interesting about him is the degree to which he's also very French.
sentences.zh: 但我认为关于他有趣的一点是，他在多大程度上也是一个非常“法国”的人。

sentences.en: And because, you know, Martinique was, you know, French colony.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，马提尼克是，你知道，法国殖民地。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to do this topic because I read a fantastic essay by Tom Owolade in Unheard on Fanon.
sentences.zh: 所以我想做这个主题，因为我在《Unheard》上读到了汤姆·奥沃拉德写的一篇关于法农的精彩文章。

sentences.en: And the moment I read it, I messaged him and asked him if he would come on and elaborate not just about Fanon, but about the entire history of African decolonisation.
sentences.zh: 我读完的那一刻，就给他发了信息，邀请他来节目，不仅要详细谈谈法农，还要谈谈整个非洲非殖民化的历史。

sentences.en: So Tom, thanks very much for answering the question.
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆，非常感谢你回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Yes, your entire history.
sentences.zh: 是的，你的全部历史。

sentences.en: We've got, what, 50 minutes, 40, 50 minutes to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们有，多少，50分钟，40、50分钟来完成这个。

sentences.en: So thanks so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: So Tom, could I ask you, December 1958, when Fanon delivers those comments, what is the state of play with Africa and the process of decolonisation?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我想问你，1958年12月法农发表那些评论时，非洲和非殖民化进程的现状如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, so in 1958, decolonisation was just at the very early stages.
sentences.zh: 是的，1958年时，非殖民化才刚刚处于起步阶段。

sentences.en: So a year before that, in 1957, the first black African country to gain independence from the British Empire was Ghana with Kwame Nkrumah.
sentences.zh: 在那之前的一年，即1957年，加纳在夸梅·恩克鲁玛的领导下，成为第一个从大英帝国获得独立的黑人非洲国家。

sentences.en: And the year before that, in 1956, two of France's protectorates in Northern Africa, Tunisia and Morocco, gained independence.
sentences.zh: 而在那之前的一年，即1956年，法国在北非的两个保护国——突尼斯和摩洛哥——获得了独立。

sentences.en: But by 1945, which I think should be seen as the year in which many anti-colonial leaders really gained confidence,
sentences.zh: 但到1945年，我认为这一年应该被视为许多反殖民领导人真正获得信心的一年，

sentences.en: there were about only four African countries that could be said to be independent.
sentences.zh: 当时只有大约四个非洲国家可以说得上是独立的。

sentences.en: So Egypt, which we can dispute, but was arguably an independent state by 1945.
sentences.zh: 比如埃及，虽然我们可以争论，但到1945年它可以说是一个独立国家。

sentences.en: But very much, I mean, had long been under British funds, hadn't it?
sentences.zh: 但很大程度上，我是说，它长期以来一直处于英国的资金控制下，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, Ethiopia as well, which was, of course, occupied during the Second World War by Mussolini's Italy.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有埃塞俄比亚，当然，它在第二次世界大战期间被墨索里尼的意大利占领过。

sentences.en: Liberia, which was founded in the 19th century by ex-African-American slaves or was founded for, I should say, ex-African-American slaves in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 利比里亚，它是由前非裔美国奴隶在19世纪建立的，或者我应该说，是为前非裔美国奴隶建立的。

sentences.en: And also Sierra Leone, which was founded to house slaves that were freed after the American Revolutionary War.
sentences.zh: 还有塞拉利昂，它是为了安置美国独立战争后被解放的奴隶而建立的。

sentences.en: South Africa as well was independent because in 1910, South Africa became a dominion within the British Empire,
sentences.zh: 南非也是独立的，因为1910年南非成为了大英帝国的一个自治领，

sentences.en: which meant similar to Australia and also Canada, it's had independence and was self-governing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它和澳大利亚以及加拿大一样，拥有独立地位并且实行自治。

sentences.en: So apart from those countries, Africa was colonized or at least controlled by some other means by European powers.
sentences.zh: 所以除了这些国家，非洲要么被殖民，要么至少通过其他方式被欧洲列强控制。

sentences.en: And well, there's quite a lot of there's quite a lot of variety in that, though, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其中有相当多的多样性，不是吗？

sentences.en: So some of these places have, let's say, French Algeria or Kenya or, let's say, southern Rhodesia.
sentences.zh: 有些地方，比如法属阿尔及利亚、肯尼亚或者南罗得西亚，

sentences.en: They have pretty substantial European white settler populations.
sentences.zh: 它们有相当多的欧洲白人定居者人口。

sentences.en: I mean, Algeria is probably the classic example.
sentences.zh: 我是说，阿尔及利亚可能就是最典型的例子。

sentences.en: Ten percent of them are white Europeans.
sentences.zh: 百分之十的人口是欧洲白人。

sentences.en: But that's not the case everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但这并非到处都是如此。

sentences.en: So obviously there are quite a lot of colonies where there's a pretty small European presence.
sentences.zh: 显然有很多殖民地，那里的欧洲人存在感很小。

sentences.en: And there, I guess, does it depend largely on collaborationist kind of elites?
sentences.zh: 在那里，我想，这在很大程度上取决于合作主义式的精英吗？

sentences.en: I mean, collaborationist is a very loaded word, but you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 我是说，“合作主义”是一个非常沉重的词，但你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: It's basically depend.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是依赖。

sentences.en: Is the power base of the Europeans always more fragile than it looks, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为欧洲人的权力基础是否总是比看起来更脆弱？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: In a country like the Gold Coast, which later became Ghana, it was very much dependent upon the collaboration between the British colonial authorities
sentences.zh: 在像黄金海岸（后来成为加纳）这样的国家，它在很大程度上依赖于英国殖民当局

sentences.en: and the native African elites, so the businessmen and the lawyers as well.
sentences.zh: 与当地非洲精英，即商人和律师之间的合作。

sentences.en: So by 1951, for example, six years before the Gold Coast became independent as Ghana, they were given what was known as responsible self-government.
sentences.zh: 所以到1951年，也就是黄金海岸作为加纳独立的前六年，他们获得了所谓的“负责任的自治”。

sentences.en: So a constitution granted them responsible self-government.
sentences.zh: 所以宪法授予了他们负责任的自治权。

sentences.en: And this was only done because I think by that time, Ghana itself had an emerging upper middle class elite.
sentences.zh: 这之所以能实现，是因为我认为到那时，加纳本身已经出现了一个新兴的中上层精英阶级。

sentences.en: It was probably the most educated out of all of Britain's West African colonies.
sentences.zh: 它可能是英国所有西非殖民地中受教育程度最高的。

sentences.en: So the British could afford to give them a degree of autonomy on that basis.
sentences.zh: 因此，英国人可以在此基础上给予他们一定程度的自治权。

sentences.en: But that's not the case, for example, if we compare that to Congo under the Belgian colonial authority,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们将其与比利时殖民当局统治下的刚果相比，情况就并非如此，

sentences.en: which was basically ruled from Brussels, essentially, and was a very, very poorly educated colony.
sentences.zh: 刚果基本上是从布鲁塞尔统治的，而且是一个受教育程度非常、非常低的殖民地。

sentences.en: So are there radical differences between, say, how British colonies, Belgian colonies, French colonies that you can trace?
sentences.zh: 那么，在英国殖民地、比利时殖民地、法国殖民地之间，是否存在你可以追溯的根本差异？

sentences.en: Or do they, are they, I mean, I suppose there's a big difference, say, between Gold Coast and South Africa, as Dominic's pointed out.
sentences.zh: 或者说，正如多米尼克指出的那样，黄金海岸和南非之间存在巨大差异？

sentences.en: So with regards to France, the French colonies were treated as a sort of integral part of France itself, essentially.
sentences.zh: 关于法国，法国殖民地基本上被视为法国本土的一个组成部分。

sentences.en: So Algeria is, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔及利亚是，对吧？

sentences.en: Algeria is actually, I mean, it's the metropolitan part of France, yeah.
sentences.zh: 阿尔及利亚实际上，我是说，它是法国的大都市部分，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，没错，没错。

sentences.en: And even the three of the most northern Algerian territories, so Algiers, Iran and Constantine, were actually departments of France.
sentences.zh: 甚至三个最北部的阿尔及利亚领土，即阿尔及尔、奥兰和君士坦丁，实际上都是法国的省份。

sentences.en: They had the same political and legal status as actual territories within metropolitan France.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有与法国本土领土相同的政治和法律地位。

sentences.en: And the other territories as well, so in West Africa, but also in an area known as French Equatorial Africa, they were treated as part of a greater France, essentially.
sentences.zh: 其他领土也是如此，比如在西非，以及被称为法属赤道非洲的地区，它们基本上都被视为大法国的一部分。

sentences.en: Whereas with the British colonies, they were ruled as individual and independent colonies.
sentences.zh: 而英国殖民地则是作为独立且个别的殖民地来统治的。

sentences.en: So they had no sort of relation with each other.
sentences.zh: 所以它们之间没有任何关系。

sentences.en: But with France, they were all sort of integrated within greater France.
sentences.zh: 但对于法国，它们都被整合到了大法国之中。

sentences.en: And with Belgium, Belgium is an interesting case because before Congo officially became a part of the Belgian colony in 1908,
sentences.zh: 比利时的情况很有趣，因为在1908年刚果正式成为比利时殖民地之前，

sentences.en: it was essentially the private property of Leopold II, who was one of the most influential figures in the scramble for Africa.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是利奥波德二世的私有财产，他是瓜分非洲最有影响力的人物之一。

sentences.en: And he ruled Belgium for about 23 years.
sentences.zh: 他统治比利时大约23年。

sentences.en: And he basically used Belgium to extract the natural resources, especially in the 1890s, when the invention of the pneumatic title led to a massive boom for rubber.
sentences.zh: 他基本上利用比利时来掠夺自然资源，特别是在19世纪90年代，充气轮胎的发明导致了橡胶的巨大繁荣。

sentences.en: And his regime is very notorious because half the population of Congo were killed during his 23-year rule.
sentences.zh: 他的政权非常臭名昭著，因为在他23年的统治期间，刚果一半的人口被杀害了。

sentences.en: And he's also the figure upon which Kurtz, from Joseph Conrad's famous novella, Hearts of Darkness, is based upon.
sentences.zh: 他也是约瑟夫·康拉德著名中篇小说《黑暗之心》中库尔茨这一人物的原型。

sentences.en: The horror, the horror.
sentences.zh: 恐怖啊，恐怖。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, because that's, I mean, kind of hands being chopped off and people's children being killed.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为那是，我是说，砍掉手，杀害人们的孩子。

sentences.en: I mean, horrendous.
sentences.zh: 我是说，太可怕了。

sentences.en: So there's a wide array of colonial approaches to Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以欧洲人对非洲的殖民方式多种多样。

sentences.en: By the Europeans.
sentences.zh: 由欧洲人实施的。

sentences.en: But by 1958, the foundations are starting to wobble.
sentences.zh: 但到了1958年，这些基础开始动摇了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Is that due to European weakness or to the growing strength of African determination to obtain autonomy and independence, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是由于欧洲的衰弱，还是由于非洲人争取自治和独立的决心日益增强？

sentences.en: What's more important?
sentences.zh: 哪个更重要？

sentences.en: I think that's probably a case-by-case basis.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能需要具体情况具体分析。

sentences.en: So should we look at Ghana, where this, you know, this first conference of the Union of African Nations is being held in 1958?
sentences.zh: 那么我们应该看看加纳，1958年首届非洲国家联盟会议就在那里举行？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what's the process by which Ghana becomes independent from Britain?
sentences.zh: 那么加纳从英国获得独立的进程是怎样的？

sentences.en: In 1947, there was a new party that was created in Ghana.
sentences.zh: 1947年，加纳成立了一个新政党。

sentences.en: And this party was known as the United Gold Coast Convention.
sentences.zh: 这个党被称为“黄金海岸统一大会党”。

sentences.en: And it was a party which consisted of Native African elites, so businessmen and lawyers.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由当地非洲精英组成的政党，即商人和律师。

sentences.en: And the leader of that party was a man called Joseph Dwankwa.
sentences.zh: 该党的领导人是一个叫约瑟夫·丹夸的人。

sentences.en: And Dwankwa was, I believe, the first Black African to actually qualify as a barrister in the Inner Temple in London.
sentences.zh: 我相信丹夸是第一个在伦敦内殿律师学院获得大律师资格的黑人非洲人。

sentences.en: So this party consisted largely of westernised Native Africans.
sentences.zh: 所以这个党主要由西化的当地非洲人组成。

sentences.en: And the party was created so that the British could develop a path by which the Gold Coast can gradually become a self-governing country within the British Empire and possibly become independent eventually.
sentences.zh: 该党的成立是为了让英国人能够开辟一条道路，使黄金海岸能够逐渐成为大英帝国境内的一个自治国家，并最终可能实现独立。

sentences.en: And two years after the party was created, one of the leaders of the parties or one of the organisers of the parties split off and created his own party.
sentences.zh: 在该党成立两年后，该党的领导人之一或组织者之一分裂出去，成立了自己的政党。

sentences.en: And this organiser within the party was Kwame Nkrumah, who later became the first Prime Minister of Ghana.
sentences.zh: 党内的这位组织者就是夸梅·恩克鲁玛，他后来成为了加纳的第一任总理。

sentences.en: So prior to joining this party in 1947, Nkrumah lived for over a decade abroad.
sentences.zh: 在1947年加入该党之前，恩克鲁玛在国外生活了十多年。

sentences.en: He was in America studying sociology, economics and philosophy.
sentences.zh: 他在美国学习社会学、经济学和哲学。

sentences.en: But he was largely impoverished during this time.
sentences.zh: 但在此期间他基本上处于贫困状态。

sentences.en: And he even spent some time in New York selling fish.
sentences.zh: 他甚至在纽约卖过一段时间的鱼。

sentences.en: And he also later moved to London to study law.
sentences.zh: 后来他还搬到伦敦学习法律。

sentences.en: And he spent most of his time, rather than actually getting his law degree, arguing with communists and anti-colonialists in Camden cafes.
sentences.zh: 他大部分时间不是在攻读法律学位，而是在卡姆登的咖啡馆里与共产主义者和反殖民主义者争论。

sentences.en: Never go to Camden.
sentences.zh: 永远不要去卡姆登。

sentences.en: That's the lesson there.
sentences.zh: 这就是教训。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So in 1949, Nkrumah split off from the United Gold Coast Convention to set up his own party.
sentences.zh: 所以1949年，恩克鲁玛从黄金海岸统一大会党分裂出来，成立了自己的政党。

sentences.en: And the priority for Nkrumah was not independence as a gradual process.
sentences.zh: 恩克鲁玛的首要任务不是渐进式的独立。

sentences.en: He wanted independence now.
sentences.zh: 他想要立即独立。

sentences.en: He was later imprisoned by the Governor General of the Gold Coast, Charles Arden Clark, for incitement and sedition.
sentences.zh: 他后来被黄金海岸总督查尔斯·阿登·克拉克以煽动和叛乱罪监禁。

sentences.en: During his imprisonment, he actually won an election.
sentences.zh: 在他入狱期间，他实际上赢得了一场选举。

sentences.en: So in 1951, there was an important election in the Gold Coast,
sentences.zh: 所以1951年，黄金海岸举行了一场重要的选举，

sentences.en: which Nkrumah won and which basically demonstrated to the British authorities that independence was basically around the corner.
sentences.zh: 恩克鲁玛赢得了选举，这基本上向英国当局证明了独立指日可待。

sentences.en: So let me ask you two things.
sentences.zh: 那么让我问你两件事。

sentences.en: I can see Tom wants to butt in.
sentences.zh: 我看得出汤姆想插话。

sentences.en: So I'm going to ask two questions to stop him.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算问两个问题来阻止他。

sentences.en: The first one is about education.
sentences.zh: 第一个是关于教育。

sentences.en: So Nkrumah has gone to New York, and I think he studied in Pennsylvania before he went to New York, Lincoln University, and then he goes to the LSE.
sentences.zh: 恩克鲁玛去了纽约，我想他在去纽约之前在宾夕法尼亚州的林肯大学学习过，然后去了伦敦政治经济学院。

sentences.en: And if you look at a lot of these African independence leaders in the 50s and 60s, an awful lot of them have studied abroad or studied in the metropolis.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看50年代和60年代许多这些非洲独立领导人，他们中有相当多的人在国外或在大都市学习过。

sentences.en: And I wondered if you could talk a bit about the influence of that and then how representative that makes them of the people they want to lead, basically.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能不能谈谈这种影响，以及这使他们在多大程度上能代表他们想要领导的人民。

sentences.en: And then the second issue is about one thing we haven't talked about is the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是关于我们还没有谈到的一件事，那就是第二次世界大战。

sentences.en: And presumably that had a shattering effect on these, on the self-confidence of the Europeans, but also the confidence of the African.
sentences.zh: 据推测，这对欧洲人的自信心，以及非洲人的自信心，都产生了粉碎性的影响。

sentences.en: Well, the African population now knew that these people weren't, I mean, if they'd ever thought it, that these people are beatable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非洲民众现在知道这些人并不是，我是说，如果他们曾经这样想过的话，这些人是可以被打败的。

sentences.en: You know, they're not superheroes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们不是超级英雄。

sentences.en: They have feet of clay and they've been humiliated by the Japanese, for example.
sentences.zh: 他们有泥足，而且他们被日本人羞辱过，例如。

sentences.en: So there's two things there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有两件事。

sentences.en: Can you say something about those two?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这两点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以，可以。

sentences.en: And then Tom can never speak again.
sentences.zh: 然后汤姆就再也不能说话了。

sentences.en: Tom, hold on.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，等等。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: I know my place.
sentences.zh: 我知道我的位置。

sentences.en: So during the interwar period, yes, many anti-colonial leaders moved to the US and the UK to study.
sentences.zh: 在两次世界大战期间，是的，许多反殖民领导人移居美国和英国学习。

sentences.en: And I think this relates actually to the notion of pan-Africanism.
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上与泛非主义的概念有关。

sentences.en: What many people, I'm not sure, understand is that pan-Africanism is in many respects a Western concept.
sentences.zh: 很多人不确定是否理解的是，泛非主义在许多方面是一个西方概念。

sentences.en: So the very first pan-African conference, for instance, was actually held in London in 1900.
sentences.zh: 例如，第一届泛非会议实际上是1900年在伦敦举行的。

sentences.en: And it wasn't actually organized by an African.
sentences.zh: 而且它实际上并非由非洲人组织。

sentences.en: It was organized by a West Indian man called Henry Sylvester WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 它是由一位名叫亨利·西尔维斯特·威廉姆斯的西印度群岛人组织的。
zh_words: 亨利·西尔维斯特·威廉姆斯

sentences.en: And pan-African congresses were held in Paris, London, New York, and Manchester before they actually reached an African city.
sentences.zh: 泛非大会在到达非洲城市之前，实际上已经在巴黎、伦敦、纽约和曼彻斯特举行过了。

sentences.en: So the very first pan-African conference that was held in Africa wasn't until 1974.
sentences.zh: 所以，在非洲举行的第一次泛非会议直到1974年才召开。

sentences.en: Wow, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 哇，那太令人惊讶了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's incredible.
sentences.zh: 没错，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: In Dar es Salaam.
sentences.zh: 在达累斯萨拉姆。

sentences.en: So when these anti-colonial leaders moved to major Western cities, they were also interacting with West Indian thinkers and intellectuals as well.
sentences.zh: 所以当这些反殖民领袖移居到西方大城市时，他们也与西印度群岛的思想家和知识分子进行了交流。

sentences.en: So like Fanon.
sentences.zh: 就像法农那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, so like Fanon, but also like, for instance, C.L.R.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像法农，但也包括像C.L.R.这样的人。

sentences.en: James in London.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦的詹姆斯。

sentences.en: So they were interacting with these West Indian thinkers and intellectuals.
sentences.zh: 所以他们与这些西印度群岛的思想家和知识分子进行了互动。

sentences.en: And incidentally, Marcus Garvey never visited Africa in his life.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，马库斯·加维一生从未去过非洲。

sentences.en: And Garvey was one of the most influential pan-African leaders.
sentences.zh: 而加维是最具影响力的泛非领袖之一。

sentences.en: So to that extent, many of these anti-colonial leaders were, to a significant extent, Westernized.
sentences.zh: 因此，在很大程度上，这些反殖民领袖在很大程度上是西化的。

sentences.en: And they were Westernized to an extent that sort of, that essentially distinguished them from the native population of the country from which they came from.
sentences.zh: 他们的西化程度在某种程度上使他们与他们所来自国家的本土人口区别开来。

sentences.en: Because most of the population, most of the population, populations in the countries from which they came were largely illiterate.
sentences.zh: 因为他们所来自国家的大多数人口基本上都是文盲。

sentences.en: And they couldn't speak the European languages.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不会说欧洲语言。

sentences.en: And I think one of the most distinctive qualities of many of these post-colonial and anti-colonial African leaders was their fluency and was their charisma.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多这些后殖民和反殖民非洲领袖最显著的品质之一就是他们的流利表达和个人魅力。

sentences.en: And somebody like Leopold Sedat-Senghor, who was both an influential figure within the negritude movement in 1930s Paris, but also became the first president of Senegal.
sentences.zh: 比如利奥波德·塞达·桑戈尔，他既是20世纪30年代巴黎“黑人性”运动中的重要人物，也成为了塞内加尔的第一任总统。

sentences.en: And he was elected a fellow of the Académie Française, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他还是法兰西学术院的院士，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: The first black African to be elected a member of the Académie Française.
sentences.zh: 第一位当选法兰西学术院院士的黑人非洲人。

sentences.en: And he was also the first person to pass Aggregation, which is like a very competitive exam that allows you to become a teacher in France.
sentences.zh: 他也是第一个通过法国教师资格会考的人，那是一项竞争非常激烈的考试，通过后才能在法国当老师。

sentences.en: He was also a school teacher in France during the 1930s, and also a poet as well.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪30年代也曾在法国当过学校老师，同时也是一位诗人。

sentences.en: I mean, we opened with Fanon, and I commented on when I read him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们以法农开场，我也评论过我读他作品时的感受。

sentences.en: I mean, he feels to me incredibly French.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他给人的感觉非常“法国”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So many of his attitudes, his assumptions, his arguments are French.
sentences.zh: 他的许多态度、假设和论点都是法国式的。

sentences.en: And you mentioned C.L.R.
sentences.zh: And you mentioned C.L.R.

sentences.en: James, you know, this brilliant writer from the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯，你知道，这位来自加勒比海的天才作家。

sentences.en: And I read him because he writes about cricket.
sentences.zh: 我读他的作品是因为他写板球。

sentences.en: And when I read him when I was young, I thought, oh, this is, you know, he's very radical.
sentences.zh: 我年轻时读他的时候，心想，哦，这，你知道，他非常激进。

sentences.en: You know, this is most unlike any writing about cricket I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这和我读过的任何关于板球的文章都大不相同。

sentences.en: And I read him again recently, and I thought, God, this guy's British.
sentences.zh: 最近我又读了一遍，心想，天哪，这家伙是个英国人。

sentences.en: He's going on about W.G.
sentences.zh: 他一直在谈论W.G.

sentences.en: Grace all the time.
sentences.zh: 格雷斯。

sentences.en: And I guess that's kind of probably true if you're coming from the Caribbean, because they've been shaped for so much longer by British and French traditions of imperialism.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你来自加勒比地区，这大概是真的，因为他们受英国和法国帝国主义传统的影响时间要长得多。

sentences.en: And Africa, you know, the period of British and French rule is actually pretty short, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而非洲，你知道，英国和法国统治的时期其实很短，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In many of these places, it's a few decades.
sentences.zh: 在许多这些地方，只有几十年。

sentences.en: And yet it does seem, you know, both with Nkrumah and Senghor, who you've mentioned, that an awful lot of what is motivating them is coming from the universities of London, Paris,
sentences.zh: 然而，无论是你提到的恩克鲁玛还是桑戈尔，他们似乎确实有很多动力来自于伦敦、巴黎的大学，

sentences.en: New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约。

sentences.en: So do you, I mean, would it be an exaggeration to say that the impetus for decolonization from Western rule is itself pretty Western?
sentences.zh: 那么，你说，如果说去殖民化以摆脱西方统治的动力本身就是非常西方的，这是否夸大其词了？

sentences.en: I think that would be a correct thing to say, because even the notion of, and this links to your book again, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我认为这样说应该是正确的，因为即使是这个概念，这又回到了你的书，汤姆。

sentences.en: Oh, don't do this.
sentences.zh: 哦，别这样。

sentences.en: Don't do this.
sentences.zh: 别这样。

sentences.en: Thank you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: I've been so...
sentences.zh: 我一直这么……

sentences.en: Well, but the notion of universal human rights is...
sentences.zh: 好吧，但普遍人权的概念是……

sentences.en: Well, Nkrumah had a, he had a, I think he got a kind of highest distinction in theology, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，恩克鲁玛有一个，我想他在神学方面获得了某种最高荣誉，不是吗？

sentences.en: He had a...
sentences.zh: 他有一个……

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And interesting enough, Nkrumah was baptised a Catholic, and he seriously considered to becoming a Jesuit priest, but then politics...
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，恩克鲁玛受洗成为天主教徒，他曾认真考虑成为一名耶稣会神父，但后来政治……

sentences.en: Christianity by other means.
sentences.zh: 换种方式的基督教。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是，绝对是。

sentences.en: And Nkrumah as well was also besotted by many, many aspects of British culture.
sentences.zh: 而且恩克鲁玛也对英国文化的许多方面非常着迷。

sentences.en: So when he became Prime Minister of Ghana in 1957, he actually visited the Queen in Balmoral, and a picture was taken of both of them until the day he died.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在1957年成为加纳总理时，他确实去巴尔莫勒尔堡拜访了女王，他们还拍了一张合影，直到他去世那天都一直留着。

sentences.en: And that picture of Nkrumah and the Queen was one of his most prized possessions.
sentences.zh: 那张恩克鲁玛和女王的照片是他最珍贵的财产之一。

sentences.en: Well, there's that very, I think, exaggerated sequence in The Crown.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得《王冠》里有一段非常夸张的片段。

sentences.en: Have you seen that where Nkrumah and the Queen dance?
sentences.zh: 你看过恩克鲁玛和女王跳舞的那一段吗？

sentences.en: They're dancing, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们在跳舞，是的。

sentences.en: That's just, that's such a Tom Holland thing to say.
sentences.zh: 这太像汤姆·霍兰会说的话了。

sentences.en: But there's kind of Western type, you know, post-French revolutionary universalism.
sentences.zh: 但确实有一种西方类型的，你知道，后法国大革命的普遍主义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, which feeds into Marxism, and that obviously is a kind of very appealing to lots of African leaders in this period.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这融入了马克思主义，在这一时期对许多非洲领袖来说显然非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: But you do also have the universalisms of Islam and Christianity, and they're also quite important.
sentences.zh: 但你也有伊斯兰教和基督教的普遍主义，它们也相当重要。

sentences.en: And one of the things I thought was really interesting when I was researching Dominion was to discover how important Ethiopia was as, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我在研究《多米尼恩》时，我发现埃塞俄比亚作为，你知道，

sentences.en: the first Christian nation before Rome.
sentences.zh: 罗马之前第一个基督教国家的重要性，我觉得这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the sense that its origins go all the way back to Solomon and the Queen of Sheba,
sentences.zh: 而且人们认为它的起源可以追溯到所罗门和示巴女王，

sentences.en: and the sense that it had preserved its independence and therefore could provide a kind of inspiration to both to kind of African nationalists and to African Christians that did not come from Europe.
sentences.zh: 并且认为它保持了独立，因此可以为非洲民族主义者和非洲基督徒提供一种并非来自欧洲的灵感。

sentences.en: And that seemed to have a kind of salience and importance that I hadn't properly understood until I began reading that.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有一种我直到开始阅读才真正理解的显著性和重要性。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Ethiopia played an integral role in the concepts of Pan-Africanism.
sentences.zh: 埃塞俄比亚在泛非主义概念中发挥了不可或缺的作用。

sentences.en: So you can even see a legacy of that in Rastafarianism, which is a sort of a melange of Pan-Africanist ideals with a sort of worship of Ethiopian monarchy.
sentences.zh: 所以你甚至可以在拉斯塔法里教中看到它的遗产，这是一种将泛非主义理想与对埃塞俄比亚君主制的崇拜混合在一起的产物。

sentences.en: Hyliss Lassie.
sentences.zh: 海尔·塞拉西。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: And even though there was even a time when to call the Black, when Black people were referred to as Ethiopians or, yeah, or Ethiopes or something like that.
sentences.zh: 甚至曾经有一段时间，黑人被称为埃塞俄比亚人，或者，是的，或者埃塞俄比亚人等等。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think, yeah, that refers to, again, the sort of integral role Ethiopia played in a sort of collective Black identity.
sentences.zh: 我认为，是的，这再次提到了埃塞俄比亚在集体黑人认同中所发挥的不可或缺的作用。

sentences.en: I think that's why Ethiopia survived in the onslaught of Mussolini during the Second World War was, I think, so important to African decolonization.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么埃塞俄比亚在第二次世界大战期间在墨索里尼的猛攻下幸存下来，对非洲去殖民化如此重要的原因。

sentences.en: Because you sort of see the twin poles, the sort of ancient African civilization against this European superpower that claims to be a sort of resurrection of the Roman Empire,
sentences.zh: 因为你看到了两个极点，古老的非洲文明对抗这个声称是罗马帝国复兴的欧洲超级大国，

sentences.en: basically, and the African civilization survived.
sentences.zh: 基本上，而非洲文明幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just before we go to a break, I have a question.
sentences.zh: 在休息之前，我有一个问题。

sentences.en: The last question I asked about the Second World War, Tom Holland very deftly steered it away from back to his book and the subject of religion.
sentences.zh: 我刚才问的关于第二次世界大战的最后一个问题，汤姆·霍兰非常巧妙地把它引回了他的书和宗教主题上。

sentences.en: So let's park the Second World War for a second.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们先把第二次世界大战放在一边。

sentences.en: Because the question I have to ask, so much of this has been about elites, about very highly educated people who've gone, you know, who are influenced by the example of Ethiopia,
sentences.zh: 因为我要问的问题是，这一切很大程度上是关于精英，关于受过高等教育的人，他们去过，你知道，他们受到埃塞俄比亚榜样的影响，

sentences.en: who have been transformed by being at universities in their 20s and 30s, who've been talking to communists in Camden, doing lots of dodgy things like that,
sentences.zh: 他们在20多岁和30多岁时在大学里经历了转变，他们和卡姆登的共产主义者交谈，做很多类似那样可疑的事情，

sentences.en: and have come back inspired with Pan-African ideals.
sentences.zh: 然后带着泛非理想回来，受到启发。

sentences.en: My question is, what about everybody else?
sentences.zh: 我的问题是，其他人呢？

sentences.en: Because obviously decolonization is partly driven by, you know, mass meetings, protest movements, insurgences, and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为显然去殖民化部分是由，你知道，群众集会、抗议运动、叛乱等等推动的。

sentences.en: What is it that explains, I mean, it can't be as simplistic as a generalized desire for freedom,
sentences.zh: 是什么解释了，我的意思是，这不可能像普遍的自由渴望那样简单，

sentences.en: but what is it that gets all these people marching and chanting and rallying behind Kwame Nkrumah and people like him and other colonists?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么让所有人游行、高呼并团结在夸梅·恩克鲁玛和像他这样的人以及其他殖民者身后呢？

sentences.en: So with Kwame Nkrumah, he was basically, actually, I think the interesting thing about Nkrumah was that even though he went to the West and attended many elite universities,
sentences.zh: 关于夸梅·恩克鲁玛，他基本上，实际上，我认为关于恩克鲁玛有趣的一点是，尽管他去了西方并就读于许多精英大学，

sentences.en: he actually came from a, not a particularly distinguished family, and the base of Nkrumah's support came from the, the sort of emerging urban workers, essentially.
sentences.zh: 他实际上来自一个并不特别显赫的家庭，恩克鲁玛的支持基础基本上来自新兴的城市工人。

sentences.en: So the trade unionists, school teachers in cities, rather than necessarily the elites of the country.
sentences.zh: 所以是工会成员、城市里的学校老师，而不是国家的精英。

sentences.en: So Nkrumah was basically able to cultivate the persona of a man of the people, rather than a sort of distant elite.
sentences.zh: 所以恩克鲁玛基本上能够培养出一种平民领袖的形象，而不是一种遥远的精英。

sentences.en: So he was able to sort of engage in that form of populism, which I think is an accurate way to describe it.
sentences.zh: 所以他能够参与那种民粹主义，我认为用这个词来描述是准确的。

sentences.en: And he was also a sort of agony aunt as well.
sentences.zh: 而且他也是某种“知心大姐”。

sentences.en: So an interesting thing about Nkrumah was that many people actually visited his residence during the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 关于恩克鲁玛有趣的一点是，在20世纪50年代，许多人实际上拜访了他的住所。

sentences.en: Asking for advice about what kind of job they can do, and also asking, asking for advice on, on marital problems as well.
sentences.zh: 询问关于他们能做什么样的工作的建议，也询问关于婚姻问题的建议。

sentences.en: Goodness, that's a, that's a level of engagement that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那是一种参与程度，是的。

sentences.en: Imagine seeing elements of this, of this podcast we've yet to explore.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，看到这个播客中我们尚未探索的元素。

sentences.en: Imagine doing that with Boris.
sentences.zh: 想象一下和鲍里斯那样做。

sentences.en: Imagine going to number 10 and asking Boris for marital advice.
sentences.zh: 想象一下去唐宁街10号问鲍里斯婚姻建议。

sentences.en: That would be terrible.
sentences.zh: 那会很糟糕。

sentences.en: Which is funny because Nkrumah was, was, was not, was, was not marriage in us during that time.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为恩克鲁玛在那个时候并没有结婚。

sentences.en: And, and, and, and unlike many, unlike many other African leaders, he had a very sort of chaste and slightly puritanical private life.
sentences.zh: 而且，与其他许多非洲领袖不同，他的私生活非常节制且略带清教徒色彩。

sentences.en: He was going to become a Jesuit, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他本来要成为一名耶稣会士，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Not surprised.
sentences.zh: 不奇怪。

sentences.en: I think we, I think we should take a break.
sentences.zh: 我想我们，我想我们应该休息一下。

sentences.en: And I think when we come back, we should look at the, the violence that surrounded quite a lot of the transfer of power.
sentences.zh: 我想当我们回来时，我们应该看看围绕权力移交的暴力事件。

sentences.en: So, you know, quite a, the British particularly were quite adept at the flummery of, you know, the Union Jack coming down and the new flag going up.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，英国人特别擅长那种仪式，你知道，米字旗降下，新旗帜升起。

sentences.en: And, and likewise, the French were, were, were very good at kind of manufacturing the idea of the Francophonie and the, the idea that nothing much had greatly changed.
sentences.zh: 同样，法国人也非常擅长制造“法语国家”的概念，以及一切都没有太大改变的想法。

sentences.en: But of course, there really were very, very violent exceptions to that.
sentences.zh: 但当然，确实存在非常、非常暴力的例外。

sentences.en: So let's look at that.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们看看那个。

sentences.en: And then perhaps could we look at Congo, which is, I mean, in a way the most brutal of the lot.
sentences.zh: 然后也许我们可以看看刚果，我的意思是，在某种程度上这是最残酷的一个。

sentences.en: So we will, we will be back with that after the break.
sentences.zh: 所以休息后我们会回来讨论那个。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: We are talking about African decolonization with Tom Owolade and we have been talking about elites.
sentences.zh: 我们正在与汤姆·奥沃拉德讨论非洲去殖民化，我们一直在讨论精英。

sentences.en: We've been talking about Camden coffee shops and now we're going to talk about violence because obviously this was often a very violent process, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论卡姆登的咖啡店，现在我们要讨论暴力，因为显然这通常是一个非常暴力的过程，不是吗？

sentences.en: The process of decolonization, the classic examples, places like Algeria, I suppose Kenya would be the most obvious British one.
sentences.zh: 去殖民化的过程，经典的例子，像阿尔及利亚这样的地方，我想肯尼亚会是英国最明显的例子。

sentences.en: It's not always violent, but, but when, when is it that you think, is it, is, is violence more likely when there are big populations of white settlers?
sentences.zh: 它并不总是暴力的，但是，但是当你，你认为什么时候，是，是有大量白人定居者时暴力更有可能发生吗？

sentences.en: Do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that definitely is the case in the, in the two classic examples.
sentences.zh: 我认为在两个经典例子中绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So Algeria and also Kenya as well.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔及利亚，还有肯尼亚。

sentences.en: But so with, with, with Algeria, I think, because you said at the beginning that Algeria, 10% of, of Algeria, Algeria's population came from Europe.
sentences.zh: 但是对于阿尔及利亚，我想，因为你在开头说阿尔及利亚，阿尔及利亚10%的人口来自欧洲。

sentences.en: So were European settlers, the Pierre Noir.
sentences.zh: 所以是欧洲定居者，即“黑脚”。

sentences.en: I think, I think the striking thing was that in Algiers, which was the biggest city in Algeria, the European population was a third of the city.
sentences.zh: 我认为令人震惊的是，在阿尔及尔，阿尔及利亚最大的城市，欧洲人口占了城市的三分之一。

sentences.en: So, so they, they, they, they had a massive presence.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们有巨大的存在感。

sentences.en: To people like Albert Camus.
sentences.zh: 像阿尔贝·加缪那样的人。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: He's the most famous example.
sentences.zh: 他是最著名的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: Definitely, definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，绝对是。

sentences.en: And interestingly enough, many of them, because I think the perception some people might think is that many of the sort of Pierre Noir European settlers came from France.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们中的许多人，因为我认为有些人可能会认为许多“黑脚”欧洲定居者来自法国。

sentences.en: And one of these elites were actually, many of them were poor and they came from other European Mediterranean countries.
sentences.zh: 而这些精英中的一些人实际上，他们中的许多人很穷，来自其他欧洲地中海国家。

sentences.en: So Spain, Greece, Italy as well.
sentences.zh: 所以西班牙、希腊，还有意大利。

sentences.en: Even Camus, Camus' mother was partly Spanish, I believe, or had Spanish ancestry.
sentences.zh: 甚至加缪，我相信加缪的母亲部分是西班牙人，或者有西班牙血统。

sentences.en: But I think that the key, the key thing that defined many of the Pierre Noir was resistance to any sort of, of decolonization or any sort of independence away from France.
sentences.zh: 但我认为定义许多“黑脚”的关键在于对任何形式的去殖民化或任何脱离法国的独立的抵制。

sentences.en: And the same was true in Rhodesia, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 罗得西亚也是如此，不是吗？

sentences.en: And obviously, I mean, in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 显然，我的意思是，在南非。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: It was more complicated.
sentences.zh: 情况更复杂。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And I think that was partly motivated by fear of living as a minority in a majority native country.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在一定程度上是出于对在本土人口占多数的国家中作为少数群体生活的恐惧。

sentences.en: And the sort of, the possibility of any sort of retribution, which was the case in both Algeria and also in Rhodesia, actually, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 以及对任何形式报复的担忧，不幸的是，阿尔及利亚和罗得西亚的情况确实都是如此。

sentences.en: So there was definitely violence on both sides.
sentences.zh: 所以双方确实都存在暴力行为。

sentences.en: So in Algeria, the most famous classic examples of the violence was the way in which collective punishment was meted out by the French colonial authorities.
sentences.zh: 在阿尔及利亚，最著名的暴力典型案例是法国殖民当局实施集体惩罚的方式。

sentences.en: So all the Arab and Berber populations were essentially quarantined within parts of the city and any sort of anyone suspected of sedition or terrorism was violently tortured.
sentences.zh: 当时所有的阿拉伯人和柏柏尔人基本上都被隔离在城市的部分区域内，任何被怀疑煽动叛乱或从事恐怖活动的人都会遭到残酷的折磨。

sentences.en: But there was also, from about 1955, the FLN, which was the guerrilla organization behind the Algerian independence movement.
sentences.zh: 但从1955年左右开始，阿尔及利亚民族解放阵线（FLN）出现了，这是阿尔及利亚独立运动背后的游击组织。

sentences.en: To which Fanon belonged, right?
sentences.zh: 法农也是其中的成员，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, he belonged to as well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，他也是成员之一。

sentences.en: Also targeted, specifically targeted civilian areas with European people living there.
sentences.zh: 他们还专门针对欧洲人居住的平民区进行袭击。

sentences.en: Well, there's those famous scenes in the film, The Battle of Algiers, of the people planting the bombs in the cafes, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 电影《阿尔及利亚之战》里有那些著名的场景，就是人们在咖啡馆里放置炸弹，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, that brilliant film, actually, about the violence and the sort of difficulty of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那部出色的电影，真实地展现了暴力及其带来的困境。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the film was released only in 1966.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且这部电影直到1966年才上映。

sentences.en: So just like literally just four years after the war ended, and it was actually banned in France for about five years.
sentences.zh: 也就是战争结束后仅仅四年，而且它在法国实际上被禁映了大约五年。

sentences.en: And I mean, the argument of Wretched of the Earth, Fanon's great book is precisely that there needs to be violence if European colonialism is going to be cast off.
sentences.zh: 法农的伟大著作《全世界受苦的人》的核心论点正是：如果想要摆脱欧洲殖民主义，就必须诉诸暴力。

sentences.en: Yeah, because Fanon thought that the nature of colonialism and imperialism was violent by its very nature.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为法农认为殖民主义和帝国主义的本质就是暴力的。

sentences.en: So the only adequate response to it was through violent means.
sentences.zh: 因此，应对它的唯一有效手段就是暴力。

sentences.en: Okay, which brings us to Congo, which is notoriously the worst example of European colonialism.
sentences.zh: 好的，这让我们谈到了刚果，它被公认为欧洲殖民主义最糟糕的例子。

sentences.en: And I guess you would say, I mean, it's not a coincidence then that its fate in independence is kind of awful as well.
sentences.zh: 我想你会说，它在独立后的命运也如此悲惨，这并非巧合。

sentences.en: Yeah, so in contrast to many other colonial states in Congo, the native black population were before independence.
sentences.zh: 是的，与许多其他殖民地国家相比，在独立前，刚果的黑人原住民人口处于一种特殊状态。

sentences.en: They were forbidden to become lawyers or doctors or architects, and they were also forbidden to gain any sort of senior position in the military.
sentences.zh: 他们被禁止成为律师、医生或建筑师，也被禁止在军队中担任任何高级职位。

sentences.en: So the population was not only sort of disenfranchised politically, but they were forbidden any sort of route to gaining power.
sentences.zh: 所以，当地民众不仅在政治上被剥夺了权利，而且被切断了任何获取权力的途径。

sentences.en: So when the Congo became independent, there was no civil society that was able to sort of successfully carry the country to any sort of prosperity or even sustainability,
sentences.zh: 因此，当刚果独立时，根本没有一个能够成功带领国家走向繁荣甚至可持续发展的公民社会，

sentences.en: because the population was largely illiterate.
sentences.zh: 因为绝大多数人口都是文盲。

sentences.en: But also the Belgians just, they just pack up and go.
sentences.zh: 而且比利时人只是简单地收拾行李就走了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's unbelievable when you actually read the timeline.
sentences.zh: 当你读到那个时间表时，简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: They're sort of vaguely talking about leaving in 1959.
sentences.zh: 他们在1959年还在含糊其辞地谈论离开的事。

sentences.en: They have a meeting in January 1960, and they say, we're off in the summer.
sentences.zh: 1960年1月他们开了一个会，然后说，我们夏天就走。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: You know, fend for yourselves.
sentences.zh: 你们自己看着办吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And even like during the final speech, the king of Belgium at that time, King Padua, basically praised King Leopold II for bringing the Belgians to Congo.
sentences.zh: 甚至在最后的演讲中，当时的比利时国王博杜安，基本上还在称赞利奥波德二世国王将比利时人带到了刚果。

sentences.en: And Patrice Lumumba, in a speech after said, we are not your monkeys anymore.
sentences.zh: 而帕特里斯·卢蒙巴在随后的演讲中说，我们不再是你们的猴子了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So tell us about Lumumba.
sentences.zh: 那么给我们讲讲卢蒙巴吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Who is he?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: Where's he coming from?
sentences.zh: 他从哪里来？

sentences.en: Because he's a key and tragic figure.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一个关键且悲剧性的人物。

sentences.en: He's the great martyr, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是伟大的烈士，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: He's the great martyr of decolonization, you could plausibly say.
sentences.zh: 你可以理直气壮地说，他是去殖民化运动中伟大的烈士。

sentences.en: So Lumumba was born in 1925, which, funny enough, was also the year that Fanon was born in.
sentences.zh: 卢蒙巴出生于1925年，有趣的是，那也是法农出生的年份。

sentences.en: And he became a sort of trade unioniSt.
sentences.zh: 他后来成为了一名工会成员。

sentences.en: And by 1960, he was a leader of a particular party in Congo.
sentences.zh: 到了1960年，他已经是刚果某个政党的领导人了。

sentences.en: So I think what's important to emphasize is that Congo was a vast country and there were many parties competing during the elections that led to Congo's independence.
sentences.zh: 我认为需要强调的是，刚果是一个幅员辽阔的国家，在导致刚果独立的选举中，有许多政党在竞争。

sentences.en: And Lumumba was just one of a vast array.
sentences.zh: 而卢蒙巴只是众多竞争者中的一员。

sentences.en: So he had to handle a coalition, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上必须处理一个联合政府。

sentences.en: And so by late June of 1960, Lumumba becomes the first prime minister of an independent Congo.
sentences.zh: 到了1960年6月下旬，卢蒙巴成为了独立刚果的第一任总理。

sentences.en: And the non-executive president was a man called Joseph Kasafubu, who would later play an influential role.
sentences.zh: 而非行政总统是约瑟夫·卡萨武布，他后来发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: And in this time, Lumumba's secretary of state, when he became prime minister, was a man called Joseph Desiree Mobutu.
sentences.zh: 当时，卢蒙巴担任总理时的国务秘书是一个叫约瑟夫·德西雷·蒙博托的人。

sentences.en: And now Mobutu, before I became Lumumba's private secretary, he was a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 在成为卢蒙巴的私人秘书之前，蒙博托是一名记者。

sentences.en: But before that, he served in the Congolese armed forces.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，他曾在刚果武装部队服役。

sentences.en: But he was only allowed to serve in lowly positions.
sentences.zh: 但他只被允许担任低级职位。

sentences.en: He wasn't allowed to ascend through the ranks because that was explicitly forbidden for black Africans.
sentences.zh: 他无法晋升，因为这被明确禁止黑人非洲人参与。

sentences.en: So by late June 1960, Lumumba's prime minister, but two forms of crisis were about to engulf him.
sentences.zh: 所以到了1960年6月下旬，卢蒙巴虽然当上了总理，但两种危机即将吞噬他。

sentences.en: The first crisis was the mutiny led by the Congolese armed forces, because they were still largely white, essentially.
sentences.zh: 第一场危机是刚果武装部队发动的兵变，因为军队本质上仍然主要是白人掌控。

sentences.en: And they were opposed to Lumumba from the start.
sentences.zh: 他们从一开始就反对卢蒙巴。

sentences.en: So Lumumba dismissed them.
sentences.zh: 所以卢蒙巴解雇了他们。

sentences.en: And the second crisis was a secessionist movement in the southeast of Congo, the Katanga region, which was where a lot of the diamonds were stored in Congo.
sentences.zh: 第二场危机是刚果东南部加丹加地区的分裂运动，那里储存着刚果大量的钻石。

sentences.en: And Lumumba was frightened of both the mutiny and the secessionist movement.
sentences.zh: 卢蒙巴对兵变和分裂运动都感到恐惧。

sentences.en: And that's why he actually called for the UN to come in and intervene.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他请求联合国介入干预。

sentences.en: And then Lumumba got frustrated with the UN.
sentences.zh: 后来卢蒙巴对联合国感到失望。

sentences.en: And eventually he did probably the biggest mistake that he could possibly do, which was ask for the Soviet Union to come in and intervene.
sentences.zh: 最终他可能犯下了他所能犯下的最大错误，那就是请求苏联介入干预。

sentences.en: And that was his downfall.
sentences.zh: 而这导致了他的垮台。

sentences.en: And this is when Eisenhower is the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时艾森豪威尔是美国总统。

sentences.en: president.
sentences.zh: 几年前，艾森豪威尔在苏伊士运河事件中有效地终结了英法帝国时代。

sentences.en: And Eisenhower, a few years earlier, had effectively pulled the curtain down on the British and French imperial period at Suez.
sentences.zh: 但现在他说我们必须除掉这家伙。

sentences.en: But now he's saying we've got to get rid of this guy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他实际上就是这么说的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he effectively says that, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他差不多就是说我们必须不惜一切代价除掉他。

sentences.en: He kind of says we've got to do whatever is necessary to get rid of him.
sentences.zh: 有很多解密的军情六处和中央情报局文件显示，你知道，理想情况下我们应该杀了他。

sentences.en: There's lots of declassified MI6 and CIA documents that say, you know, ideally we should kill him.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 因为他们基本上把卢蒙巴看作第二个菲德尔·卡斯特罗。

sentences.en: Because they saw Lumumba as basically a second Fidel Castro, essentially.
sentences.zh: 一个反殖民领袖，最终会变成苏联的附庸国。

sentences.en: Somebody who was basically an anti-colonial leader who would just become a Soviet state.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 他们有各种疯狂的计划来除掉卡斯特罗，比如著名的爆炸雪茄之类的。

sentences.en: They have all these kind of mad schemes to get rid of Castro famously with exploding cigars and things.
sentences.zh: 他们还派了一个叫兰利“死亡博士”的人，西德尼·戈特利布，他想出了一个主意，在卢蒙巴的牙膏里混入毒药，模拟小儿麻痹症的症状。

sentences.en: And they send a guy called Dr. Death of Langley, Sidney Gottlieb, who has this wheeze to mix some poison that will simulate the effects of polio in Lumumba's toothpaste.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们试过了，但没成功，因为我想那毒药过期了。

sentences.en: They tried that, but that didn't come because I think the poison ran out of its sell-by date.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合中情局的行事风格。

sentences.en: That's very CIA behaviour.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 所以，毒牙膏没起作用。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so the poison toothpaste doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 那么给我们讲讲他们最终如何除掉他的可怕故事吧。

sentences.en: So talk us through the horrible story about how they get rid of him.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·德西雷·蒙博托和约瑟夫·卡萨武布，正如我之前所说，他是刚果总统。

sentences.en: Joseph Desiree Mobutu and Joseph Kasafubu, who, as I said earlier, was the president of Congo.
sentences.zh: 他们决定，美国中情局和比利时当局都认为他们两人是帕特里斯·卢蒙巴的合适替代者。

sentences.en: They decide, they, the CIA in America and also the Belgian authorities saw both of them as suitable replacements for Patrice Lumumba.
sentences.zh: 于是他们联系了这两人，卢蒙巴作为刚果总理的统治只持续了64天。

sentences.en: And so they, they, they, they, they got in touch with both of them and, and Lumumba's rule as the prime minister of Congo lasted 64 days.
